items.title: Jinnah’s portrait and the communalisation of a cafe in Kerala
items.summary: A painting of Gandhi and Muhammad Ali Jinnah has become the centre of a communal controversy in Kerala. The artwork at Kashi Art Cafe in Fort Kochi was created by Malayali artist Riyas Komu in 2008. But a north Indian influencer questioned why the cafe displayed Jinnah’s portrait, served beef and was located in an area with a Muslim population. The controversy widened after influencer Diya Krishna commented “Sad reality” under the video and later defended herself by citing her Muslim friends and relatives. What is the story behind the artwork? And why is that defence problematic?

items.title: Theni jailbreak: Last 4 of escaped prisoners caught
items.summary: The last four of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from the District Jail at Thekkampatti in Tamil Nadu's Theni district were taken into custody on Wednesday, October 28, with the last two accused surrendering. The latest two, identified as siblings Thirupathi and Meenatchi Sundaram, surrendered at the Kudalur police station while two other accused, Regin and Ponmuthuselvam, were arrested earlier in the day. The jailbreak took place late on Monday, October 26, when the prisoners allegedly attacked prison staff and fled the premises. According to the Prison Department, the incident occurred around 10 pm when some inmates raised an alarm, claiming that a prisoner in the third block was experiencing an epileptic seizure. When Grade II warden Stalin Prabhu, who was on duty in the block, entered to check on the prisoner, the inmates who were lodged in the same cell allegedly attacked him and attempted to escape. They then allegedly confronted guards, snatched the keys, and opened the main entrance to flee the prison.
